arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API: post, update, and delete messages including threaded replies, list channels and read conversation history, create channels and invite users, and look up users by name or email. Use whenever the user asks to send, read, or manage Slack messages, channels, or users.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Read from and write to a Slack workspace through the official Web API. All
operations go through one script, `scripts/slack_api.cjs`, which handles auth,
request formatting, and agent-friendly output. For endpoint details, scopes,
Block Kit, pagination, and error codes, read `references/slack-api-reference.md`.

## Prerequisites

- **Token**: set `SLACK_TOKEN` (bot or user token) in the environment, or pass
  `--token <token>`. The script fails fast (before any network call) when no
  token is provided.
- **Node.js 18+** (uses the built-in `fetch`).
- **Scopes**: the token must have the scopes listed in the reference file
  (e.g., `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:manage`, `users:read`).

Run the script from the skill directory or with its full path, e.g.
`node <skill-dir>/scripts/slack_api.cjs <command> ...`.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Post a message
node scripts/slack_api.cjs post --channel C0123456789 --text "Hello from Gemini CLI"

# Reply in a thread
node scripts/slack_api.cjs post --channel C0123456789 --thread-ts 1712345678.000000 --text "Thread reply"

# Read the last 10 messages of a channel
node scripts/slack_api.cjs history --channel C0123456789 --limit 10

# List channels (resolve names to IDs for other commands)
node scripts/slack_api.cjs list-channels --limit 50
```

## Core Tasks

### Posting Messages

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs post --channel <id|name> --text "message" [--thread-ts <ts>] [--blocks '<json>'] [--username <name>] [--link_names] [--unfurl]
```

- `--text` is required unless `--blocks` is given; provide both for a rich
  message with a plain-text fallback.
- `--blocks` takes a Block Kit JSON array as a single quoted argument. See the
  reference file for examples and limits.
- With `--thread-ts`, the message is posted as a reply inside that thread.

### Updating and Deleting Messages

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs update --channel C0123456789 --ts 1712345678.000000 --text "new text"
node scripts/slack_api.cjs delete --channel C0123456789 --ts 1712345678.000000
```

`--ts` is the message timestamp exactly as returned by the API
(`<seconds>.<microseconds>`, a string).

### Reading Channels and History

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs list-channels [--limit 100] [--cursor <next_cursor>] [--types public_channel,private_channel]
node scripts/slack_api.cjs history --channel <id> [--limit 20] [--oldest <unix>] [--latest <unix>]
```

- Paginate with `--cursor`: outputs print `next_cursor=...` when more results
  exist; loop until it is absent.
- `history` requires a channel **ID** (resolve names with `list-channels`).

### Managing Channels and Users

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs create-channel --name releases [--private]
node scripts/slack_api.cjs invite --channel C0123456789 --users U123,U456
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users [--limit 100] [--cursor <next_cursor>]
node scripts/slack_api.cjs user-by-email --email user@example.com
```

## Script Reference

Run `node scripts/slack_api.cjs --help` for full usage. Every command exits 0
on success and 1 on failure and prints a single-line `Success:` / `Failure:`
message; long payloads are truncated so output stays readable in the agent
context window.

## Error Handling

- API failures print `Failure: <slack_error_code>` plus detail, e.g.
  `missing_scope`, `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel`, `rate_limited`.
- On `rate_limited`, back off (use the `Retry-After` value) and retry.
- A missing token is reported before any network call is made.

## References

Read `references/slack-api-reference.md` when you need:

- Token scopes per operation
- Endpoint and parameter details
- Block Kit message examples
- Pagination and rate-limit guidance
- Common error codes and their fixes

# Slack Web API Reference

Companion reference for `scripts/slack_api.cjs`. All calls go to
`https://slack.com/api/<method>` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

## Authentication and Scopes

- Tokens are workspace-scoped. Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with
  `xoxp-`. Never hardcode tokens; use `SLACK_TOKEN` or `--token`.
- A bot must be **added to a channel** before it can post to or read that
  channel (private channels and DMs too).
- Required scopes (configured on the Slack app, under OAuth & Permissions):

| Operation | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `chat.delete` | `chat:write` |
| `conversations.list` | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| `conversations.history` | `channels:history` (public), `groups:history` (private) |
| `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.invite` | `channels:manage` (or `channels:write`) |
| `users.list` | `users:read` |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `users:read.email` |

Missing scopes produce `missing_scope` errors; add the scope and reinstall the
app to the workspace.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Key parameters | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | POST | `channel`, `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts` | `channel` accepts an ID or name without `#`. `thread_ts` makes it a threaded reply. |
| `chat.update` | POST | `channel`, `ts`, `text`, `blocks` | `ts` is the message timestamp string. |
| `chat.delete` | POST | `channel`, `ts` | Only messages posted by the same token can be deleted. |
| `conversations.list` | POST | `limit` (max 1000), `cursor`, `types` | `types` e.g. `public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`. |
| `conversations.history` | POST | `channel` (ID only), `limit`, `oldest`, `latest` | `oldest`/`latest` are Unix timestamps; `latest` may be `now`. |
| `conversations.create` | POST | `name` (lowercase, ≤21 chars), `is_private` | Returns the created channel object. |
| `conversations.invite` | POST | `channel`, `users` (comma-separated IDs) | Also works for private channels and MPIMs. |
| `users.list` | POST | `limit` (max 1000), `cursor` | Includes bots and deleted users (`deleted: true`). |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | POST | `email` | Returns 404-style `users_not_found` if no match. |

## Response Format

Success: `{ "ok": true, ... }`. Failure: `{ "ok": false, "error": "<code>" }`,
sometimes with `response_metadata.messages` for extra detail. The wrapper
script prints `Success:`/`Failure:` lines and exits 0/1 accordingly.

## Pagination

- `conversations.list` and `users.list` use cursor pagination: read
  `response_metadata.next_cursor` and pass it as `--cursor` until it is empty.
  `limit` caps results per page (default 100).
- `conversations.history` pages with `has_more` + `response_metadata.next_cursor`;
  a common pattern is to pass the oldest seen `ts` as `--latest` on the next
  call. `ts` values are strings like `"1712345678.000000"` — pass them exactly.

## Block Kit Essentials

`--blocks` takes a JSON array (single quoted argument). At most 50 blocks per
message.

```json
[
  { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Release notes" } },
  { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*v2.3.0* is out :tada:" } },
  { "type": "divider" },
  {
    "type": "actions",
    "elements": [
      { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "View" }, "url": "https://example.com" }
    ]
  }
]
```

Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `actions`, `context`, `header`,
`input` (in modals), `image`. Text objects use `mrkdwn` or `plain_text`;
set `"emoji": true` on plain_text to render emoji shortcodes. Invalid blocks
return `invalid_blocks`.

## Rate Limits

- Default tier (Tier 3): about 50 requests/minute per token per method, with
  bursts of 20+ allowed.
- On `rate_limited`, the response includes `Retry-After` (seconds) — wait and
  retry with backoff.
- Pagination loops count toward the limit; keep pages large rather than many
  small calls.

## Common Errors

| Error | Meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is wrong or expired. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks the required scope; add and reinstall the app. |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel ID is wrong; resolve via `list-channels`. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot is not a member; add it to the channel first. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive or pick another. |
| `invalid_blocks` | Block Kit JSON is malformed or over limits. |
| `msg_too_long` | `text` exceeds 40,000 characters. |
| `users_not_found` | User IDs are invalid; check `users` output. |
| `rate_limited` | Back off per `Retry-After`. |
| `too_many_conversations` | `conversations.list` needs `types` or narrower scope. |

## Gotchas

- Prefer channel **IDs** everywhere; only `chat.postMessage` reliably accepts
  names. Resolve names with `list-channels`.
- `ts` values are strings, not floats — pass them exactly as returned.
- Blocks-only messages have empty `text`; always include `text` as a fallback
  for notifications and search.
- Private channels and DMs behave the same via `conversations.*`, but the bot
  must be a member.
- A token can only update/delete messages it posted.
